correspondence.component_scope: eastern chosen opening and upper urban approach
correspondence.finding: The eastern chosen opening is within a west-leading foothill drainage corridor at the eastern edge of the metropolitan basin. Its wooded valley continues through the urban fringe and southern city corridor. Haze, vegetation and the small channel width preclude bank-by-bank tracing, but the ordinary valley and receiving continuity are visible. The chosen vertex is not identified as the river’s natural spring; no exact upper hydronym is assigned.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: southern urban corridor and northward bend
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor follows the connected southern urban drainage westward, then turns north along the western metropolitan edge. Vegetated channel margins, the valley floor and the joins remain geographically continuous despite bridges and dense development. Tiribí is supported as a tributary/subbasin name by the independent hydrological study, without extending that name uniformly to every opening segment.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: northwestern urban join and larger collector
correspondence.finding: The northbound urban tributary reaches the larger, deeply incised collector at the northwestern metropolitan edge; the selection then follows its westward bend. The imagery distinguishes the joining valley from parallel northern urban tributaries. The hydrological study places combined Tiribí–Virilla drainage upstream of the Virilla station at San Miguel.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: middle incised westbound corridor to fragment boundary
correspondence.finding: West of the urban area, the selected larger collector occupies a continuous incised valley through cultivated and wooded hills, receiving side tributaries and continuing to the northern-branch junction near the fragment boundary. Dark or locally widened reaches and water-management structures do not interrupt the ordinary valley correspondence; no present operating route, exact impoundment name or hydraulic allocation is asserted.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: western junction and canyon exit
correspondence.finding: The second fragment continues from the same shared junction through the westbound receiving canyon and out toward lower-relief country. The independently read study places Virilla and Grande de San Ramón within the receiving Grande de Tárcoles system. Grande de San Ramón is a distinct joining branch, not an alias of the selected eastern upper route.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: southwestward lower floodplain
correspondence.finding: The receiving channel turns southwest across an increasingly broad agricultural and wooded floodplain. The image shows a continuous meandering river, bars and tributary approaches. The simplified stored path is treated as orientation through this corridor, without requiring its line to follow every contemporary meander.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower floodplain and estuarine approach
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues southwest through the lower alluvial corridor and widened tidal/estuarine approach. Broad bends, bars, vegetated floodplain and coastal wetland channels are visible. The main receiving passage remains continuous to the coastal mouth; side wetland channels are not promoted into separate selected branches.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: rendered terminal and distinct source end setting
correspondence.finding: The final stored part reaches the Pacific coastal mouth/estuarine receiving setting. The stored source endpoint lies slightly southwest of the displayed terminal in the same coastal receiving zone. These two endpoints are retained as distinct records; neither is moved to the imagery’s bank, bar or instantaneous waterline. The visible mouth joins the coastal ocean.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern feeder opening and eastern bend
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in a visible narrow drainage valley. The corridor bends east around low terrain, turns north and continues into the northwest-trending receiving valley. The normally completed southern-detail original shows the whole bend and its receiving passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwest feeder valley and side-stream joins
correspondence.finding: The narrow valley continues northwest through rocky uplands, receives visible side drainages and opens toward the wider alluvial corridor. The selected parts follow that connected valley setting despite generalized line offsets.

correspondence.component_scope: Join to the broader northern river corridor
correspondence.finding: The southeastern branch reaches a broad sediment-lined channel and low valley floor. The selected route then turns north through the common receiving corridor; nearby elongated lakes are retained as surrounding valley context rather than assigned the river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle river and alluvial bends
correspondence.finding: A continuous northward river corridor with bends, bars, adjoining ponds and lateral drainage joins is readable throughout the overview and its overlapping middle enlargement. The lower end is also covered by the northern original.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake-rich lowland, meander interior and eastern tributary junction
correspondence.finding: The northern detail shows a single broad connected river lowland containing many ponds and elongated lakes, a western river channel and a substantial eastern tributary loop that meets it. The generalized selected line crosses the lowland and meander interior while the visible connected river skirts waterbodies and follows wider bends. This is geographic correspondence within the shared receiving valley, not evidence that every intersected pond is a serial river-through-lake passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower river approach to the inlet
correspondence.finding: The river continues north down the broad valley, passing minor lateral drainages, and widens into the sandy coastal mouth. The lower original links the inland receiving river to the inlet-head setting described in ARC403.

correspondence.component_scope: Stored source sea terminal
correspondence.finding: The stored source terminal lies in the lower mouth/channel and sandy alluvial-fan setting at the inlet head. The northern original supports this coastal receiving correspondence independently of the rendered endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Separate rendered sea terminal
correspondence.finding: The rendered terminal extends farther toward the inlet-side sandy mouth margin than the source terminal. Both occupy the same river-to-inlet receiving setting, and ARC403 identifies the river entering Wrottesley Inlet south of Reid Point.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern opening and upper fan
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies on the mapped Gooseberry Creek fan west of the Tobin Range. Its westward and northward selected bends occupy the same open receiving fan; the model does not follow every cartographic intermittent-channel bend.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern fan to axial Spring Creek setting
correspondence.finding: The selected southwestward route passes the Jim/Cow/Sheep Creek fan mouths and reaches the Spring Creek axial valley. Original relief, contours and intermittent drainage show one continuous descending valley-floor receiving corridor; no intervening divide or separate-lake transfer is required. No exact wet thread is asserted across the dry fan interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Spring Creek upper valley and joining tributaries
correspondence.finding: Repeated direct Spring Creek labels follow the main north–south valley. Wilder/Peavine entry, Bartlett Creek and the Kennedy/Gladiator Creek joining setting are visible. Local straight blue linework occurs beside the channel; present ditch operation is not inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Pleasant Valley narrows
correspondence.finding: The selected middle route follows the Spring Creek wetland-symbol valley and its constricted southward continuation through the Pleasant Valley narrows, then opens onto the northern Dixie receiving plain.

correspondence.component_scope: Spring Creek and Jersey Valley Wash shared fan floor
correspondence.finding: The selected route traverses the broad adjoining Spring Creek–Jersey Valley Wash fan/field setting and turns southwest. Both mapped channels share the same open receiving floor, with no cartographic divide; ordinary corridor correspondence is supported without assigning Jersey Valley Wash as an alias of Spring Creek or claiming operation of local rectilinear drains.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward lower Spring Creek receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: The route crosses the continuously mapped low-gradient floor toward the mapped lower Spring Creek, then meets its southward corridor near the Cottonwood Creek fan. Detailed mapping retains direct Spring Creek labels even where the selected centerline traverses adjacent dry receiving ground.

correspondence.component_scope: Dixie Meadows and salt-marsh approach
correspondence.finding: Lower Spring Creek ends in the broad Dixie Meadows/Dixie Valley receiving floor. The selected western and southwestern extension crosses that uninterrupted lowland to the northern margin of Humboldt Salt Marsh. A blue thread through every dry portion is not required or asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected salt-marsh ending
correspondence.finding: The last stored parts lie inside the mapped Humboldt Salt Marsh receiving area. Source and rendered terminal descriptions are preserved separately; both correspond to this inland marsh/playa interior, not an ocean or an inferred outflow.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and northeastern turn
correspondence.finding: The selected opening occupies the shallow eastern-facing terrain west of Cutter, then follows the open receiving ground to the southeastern end of the Jornada Lakes setting. Source contours and relief support this ordinary descending dry corridor. The path is not assigned to a current wetted tributary or forced through the named lake polygons.

correspondence.component_scope: Hackberry and McLendon draw corridor
correspondence.finding: The southeastward upper route follows the mapped shallow Hackberry Draw and McLendon Draw terrain and continues east of Spaceport America. It stays within the broad descending draw/plain corridor, with minor tanks and roads. These bounded draw labels do not establish one whole-composite river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Aleman receiving area and Prisor Hill passage
correspondence.finding: The selected route reaches the mapped Aleman Draw pond/channel setting, then passes the western side of Prisor Hill into the southern draw/plain corridor. Mapped contours and water-linework provide the joining and local hill-passage context; current tank management or through-flow is not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Upham Hills and Jornada Draw approach
correspondence.finding: The route continues beside the Lyons Draw setting, around the western margin of Upham Hills and through the broad Jornada Draw corridor between the hills and Point of Rocks. Topography and original imagery show its connection into the central sediment/pan chain.

correspondence.component_scope: Central Jornada playa passage
correspondence.finding: These parts occupy the connected low sediment and playa complex south of the Jornada Draw label. Topography gives the pan margins and surrounding relief; actual photographic pixels show a continuous broad receiving floor through the selected bends.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern playa-floor continuation and pan chain
correspondence.finding: The originally questioned southeastward exit from the central playa is supported by the independently read imagery: the selected route remains within a continuous pale sediment/vegetated receiving swale and pan-margin corridor, passing between and around the nearby low uplands. It reaches the southeastern low ground adjoining Antelope Flat. The evidence supports ordinary dry receiving-floor correspondence, not a surveyed spill elevation, perennial connection or a blue-line channel through every segment.

correspondence.component_scope: Antelope Flat to northern Lake Tank approach
correspondence.finding: The route continues south across the broad low corridor east of the Doña Ana Hills, with small mapped pans/tanks and local roads. Contours constrain the lowland between higher ground to either side and lead to the Lake Tank depression. Adjacent Cottonwood, Goldenburg and Ropes draw labels are not promoted to selected-reach names from proximity alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual Lake Tank ending
correspondence.finding: The last stored segment ends in the northern part of the mapped Lake Tank waterbody/depression east of the Doña Ana Mountains. The source and rendered endpoint descriptions are separate and retain this inland receiving setting; neither is moved to the Río Grande or an invented external outlet.
